title: Equivalent fractions
keyIdea: Equivalent fractions are different names for the same amount.

kid: Equivalent fractions are different names for the same amount: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.
If you cut every piece into 2 smaller pieces, you get double the pieces and double the ones you take, so it's still the same amount.
adult: Multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number gives an equivalent fraction: 1/3 = 2/6 = 3/9. On a number line, equivalent fractions mark the same point.
Adding the same number to top and bottom does not work (1/2 is not 2/3). This is one of the most common fraction misconceptions.

familyTip: Fold paper strips into halves, quarters and eighths and line them up to see which lengths match.

practice.hint: The denominator went from 2 to 6. What did it get multiplied by?
Is the top exactly half of the bottom?
practice.explain: 4/8 and 5/10 are halves, but 3 is not half of 5.

practice.prompt: Ben says 1/2 = 2/3 because he added 1 to the top and the bottom. Is he right?
choices: No, you must multiply or divide both by the same number
Yes, he did the same to both
practice.hint: Compare a half and two-thirds of a cake.
practice.explain: 2/3 is bigger than 1/2. Adding the same number changes the value; multiplying both by the same number doesn't.

items.explain: Multiply the top by 2 as well: 3 × 2 = 6.

items.hint: Multiply top and bottom by the same number.

items.explain: Divide the bottom by 3 as well: 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
